info.title: API.SH: TMDB
info.description: The TMDB API from API.SH: public TMDB data as clean JSON. Every endpoint is a GET with query parameters and your key in the x-api-key header. Calls that run cost the credits shown (x-credits): successes, and lookups that found nothing (404). Refused calls and errors on our side are free. Docs: https://api.sh/docs · Every platform: https://api.sh/openapi.json

get.description:
A film on The Movie Database by id or link: title, year, tagline, overview, user score, vote average and count, certification and release (for the page's region), genres, runtime, poster and backdrop, featured crew (director, writers), top-billed cast with characters, keywords, homepage and social links, status, original title and language, budget, revenue, countries, release date, the collection id the film belongs to, the headline where-to-watch offer (`streaming`: provider, kind of offer, logo, watch link), the featured trailer (`featured_video`: site, key, name, link), media counts (videos, backdrops, posters) and the featured user review (author, date, excerpt, link). Opt in with `include` for more, each one more page read: `recommendations` (similar titles with user score), `watch_providers` (every stream, rent and buy offer in `region` with provider, price, quality and link) `videos` (trailers with type, duration, publish date, channel and link), `images` (the full backdrop, poster and logo galleries with size, language and primary flag; three pages read) and `reviews` (every user review with author, rating, date and text). TMDB's site lists recommendations only; it has no separate similar-titles list.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/tmdb-movie

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: TMDB movie id, e.g. `550` (Fight Club).

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Or a themoviedb.org/movie/... link.

parameters.name: language
parameters.description: Page language (default en-US), e.g. de-DE, fr-FR, es-ES.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Comma-separated extras, each one more page read: recommendations, watch_providers, videos, images (three pages), reviews.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: Country for `include=watch_providers`, two letters (default US), e.g. GB, DE, CA.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
The Movie Database's "What's popular" lists (streaming, on TV, for rent, in theatres) and "Free to watch" films or series: position, id, type, title, date, link and poster. Or browse every film or series with your own filters (the site's Movies and TV Shows pages): give any of `sort_by`, `with_genres`, `with_original_language`, `vote_average.gte`, `vote_average.lte`, `vote_count.gte`, `release_date.gte`, `release_date.lte` (not together with `category`); `type` is then movie (default) or tv, 20 a page with `page` and `next_page`, and the response echoes the applied `filters`.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/tmdb-popular

get.description:
A series on The Movie Database by id or link: name, first-air year, tagline, overview, user score, votes, certification, genres, poster and backdrop, creators, top cast with episode counts, keywords, links, status, type, original language, networks and the current season (rating, year, episodes, overview), number of episodes, first and last air dates, the next episode to air (`next_episode_to_air`: name, season and episode number, air date, link; or `last_episode_to_air` once nothing is scheduled), the headline where-to-watch offer (`streaming`), the featured video, media counts and the featured user review. Opt in with `include` for more, each one more page read: `seasons` (every season with number, name, year, episode count, rating, overview, poster and link), `recommendations`, `watch_providers` (every stream, rent and buy offer in `region`) `videos` (trailers), `images` (full backdrop, poster and logo galleries; three pages read), `reviews` (every user review) and `episode_runtime` (run time of each episode of the current season: the distinct run times and the average, in minutes).

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/tmdb-tv

apiKey.name: x-api-key
apiKey.description: Create keys at https://app.api.sh/keys. Authorization: Bearer <key> also works.

raw.name: raw
raw.description: 0 leaves out the bulky `raw` source blocks (often 10-30x smaller).

fields.name: fields
fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return, e.g. `posts.id,posts.title`. Call metadata is always included.

fresh.name: fresh
fresh.description: 1 skips the 24-hour cache and fetches live.

output.name: output
output.description: csv or ndjson returns the response's records (its main list, or the object as one row) as CSV or NDJSON instead of JSON.

records.name: records
records.description: With output=csv|ndjson: the top-level list to turn into rows (e.g. `reviews`), or `.` for the whole object as one row.

status_url.description: On a 503 for a paused endpoint: the status page, which lists open incidents.

E400.description: A parameter is missing or invalid. Not charged (unless the call ran and the source rejected the value; credits_used says).

E401.description: Missing, invalid, revoked or expired API key. Not charged. See https://api.sh/docs/errors#401

E402.description: Not enough credits, a spend limit you set was reached (`spend_limit`), or the key's monthly credit cap was reached (`key_cap`). Not charged.

E404.description: Not found, or not public. A lookup that ran costs the endpoint's price (credits_used says); an unknown route is free.

E502.description: The source site failed this time; retry. Not charged.

E503.description: Endpoint paused or temporarily unavailable; may include retry-after, and status_url (https://api.sh/status) for a paused endpoint. Not charged.
